correctness.rationale: The mathematical theorem survived unchanged. Independence and the positive all-zero event give weights ((c)_n/n!)^r w^n. If an iid real-valued m-fold root assigned positive probability to a negative value range, the event all summands are negative would have positive probability; hence all summands are nonnegative. The zero atom forces a zero atom for the root, and conditioning the other summands to be zero forces lattice support. For a compound Poisson or infinitely divisible law the second log coefficient must be nonnegative: the root's coefficient is p0^(1/m)(a2-(1-1/m)a1²/2)/m. Its sign in the limit is determined by ((c+1)/(2c))^r-1/2. The rational bounds 4/9 and 27/64 exclude every c,r>=2 except (2,2). At (2,2), summing (n+1)^2 gives (1+z)/(1-z)^3, so the log has intensities 4 w^k/k at odd k and 2 w^k/k at even k, a positive summable sequence. The ordinary geometric and negative binomial cases use the log series for (1-wz)^(-1) and (1-wz)^(-c). Inspected the supporting source and checker without executing uploaded code; the proof is exact and the checker's finite arithmetic is corroborative.
